title: Kotlin/Native Memory Management
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of kotlin/native memory management using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates kotlin/native memory management.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Kotlin/Native Memory Management** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Measure a reproducible workload before optimizing, and compare correctness plus CPU, memory, allocation, and target-specific costs. Use the subtopics—Native Memory Model, Garbage Collection, Interoperability with ARC—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with native memory model. Then compare it with garbage collection. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Native Memory Model
items.text: Native Memory Model should be evaluated against input size, allocation behavior, and workload. Start with a correctness test and reproducible measurement; choose the simplest implementation that meets the requirement.

items.title: Garbage Collection
items.text: Garbage Collection is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

items.title: Interoperability with ARC
items.text: Interoperability with ARC means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.code:
data class Greeting(val text: String)

fun greetingFor(name: String): Greeting = Greeting("Hello, $name")

fun main() = println(greetingFor("Kotlin").text)
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, or Kotlin/Native project configured for the selected target. Verify platform support and maturity before production use.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Kotlin/Native Memory Management removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
